note: A consumer of tj-actions/changed-files at the time of the March 2025 tag compromise (push.yml as it stood from April 2024 until after the incident): the publish-changes job resolves changed-files@v42 by tag, then publishes the npm packages through a local composite action holding NPM_TOKEN and a personal access token. The compromised tag ran with both secrets in reach. The publish step lives inside ./.github/actions/job-publish, which the workflow scan does not read, so no publishes impact is proven and the spec gives High (secrets, no impact) rather than Critical. The deploy job's own-organization deploy action, pinned by tag into an environment with AWS keys, reaches a Critical: offline no advisory is fetched, so no finding says either action is already bad and each takes a compromise of the dependency first; the deploy action's owner is the repository's own, so it is only not pinned and capped at Medium, while changed-files comes from an owner outside the authorized list, which keeps its High. The deploy job's environment is a protection, never an impact by itself: the deploy is the action's own step, a deploy action the facts read as one, so the deploy path reaches impact:deploys; its tier is the Medium cap's either way. The linkinator job runs a third-party action by tag from an owner outside the authorized list, holding the repository-default token: code execution, High. verify-example needs publish-changes for ordering alone: a bare needs hands nothing over (no artifact, cache or output read), so it is no hop of the publish-changes path and its own ISSUE-307 and ISSUE-801 count as individual findings next to the other two. Hand count: two High paths 2 x 15 = 30, one Medium path 6, four other findings (ISSUE-307 Low 2 x 2, ISSUE-801 Medium 5 x 2), so 100 - 50 = 50: D, still above the E the compromise would have asked for.
